programmes.d: Rob and Buddy find themselves overworked when Sally becomes a television personality overnight.
When Laura fills in for Sally at the office, her performance exceeds everyone's expectations.
Rob recalls the hectic time of his Army marriage to Laura.
At the insistence of an overbearing guest star, Rob takes over as producer of The Alan Brady Show.
Rob and Laura's parents compete to get the couple committed to their respective cemetery plots.
A scratch on Rob's new car causes a domestic crisis at the Petrie house.
Rob attempts to coax a legendary radio star out of retirement for a TV special.
A painting of Laura resurfaces -- but this time she is not wearing any clothes.
Rob goes to see an old Army buddy's nightclub act and winds up spending the night in jail.
Rob and Laura suspect their neighbor Jerry is having an affair.
Fearing he may be going bald, Rob tries a barber's secret recipe.
Rob is skeptical when Laura's new writing teacher thinks she shows promise.
Laura proves herself more proficient than Rob in the art of self-defense.
Rob, Laura, Sally and Buddy spend a frightening night in a haunted cabin at a mountain resort.
Rob and Laura are unaware that their teenage babysitter has a crush on Laura.
Rob's friendship with Jerry is almost destroyed in a feud over a neighbor's crabgrass.
Rob is offered a job as humor consultant at a magazine for man-about-town.
Sally Rogers is romanced by her "secret" admirer -- the owner of Monker's Delicatessen.
Rob and Laura are on their way to visit the doctor when they are trapped in a stalled elevator.
The "Alan Brady" writers entertain at a prison and Rob gets locked up with the inmates.
Rob puts his job at risk when he convinces Alan Brady to host a cultural documentary program.
Laura takes two of Millie's prescription pills and suffers disastrous side effects.
Rob tries to get a raise for Buddy and Sally from Alan Brady's tight-fisted accountant.
Rob struggles to hide his flu symptoms at a family party rather.
Rob, Sally and Buddy go on big ego trips when a national magazine wants to do a story about them.
Rob is once again forced to thwart another scheme of his old but manipulative friend, Neil Schenk.
Rob receives a ransom demand of $2,500 for his lost television script.
Rob resorts to psychological warfare to get even with a practical joker.
Rob's younger brother involves Sally Rogers in a romantic Waterloo.
Stacey Petrie tries to save his new business from closing and his romance from ending.
Millie and Laura become two terrible stage-mothers when Rob agrees to hire Ritchie for a commercial.
Rob agrees to have a popular British singing duo spend the night at his home.
Rob takes a shady salesman to court for selling Laura smelly feather pillows.
Buddy and Rob run a shoe store they've invested in after chasing off its only full-time salesman.
Rob and Laura are in a quandary over how Ritchie can protect himself from a girl.
Rob learns that a song he helped write is about to become a hit.
Rob recalls the time he and Jerry tried to buy the same house.
Sally's new boyfriend is secretive about what he does for a living.
The Petries' second honeymoon becomes a disaster when Laura's toe gets caught in a bath spout.
Rob and Laura have no choice but to wear gloves to an important community banquet.
Alan needs Rob's help improving a script for his Broadway debut.
Rob recalls his first meeting with Alan Brady during a stay-awake marathon for his disc-jockey job.
Rob buys a motorcycle and is arrested as a joyriding delinquent.
Buddy offers to help Laura get a fur coat for the wholesale price.
Laura blurts out an embarrassing secret on a national television quiz show.
Rob sets out to write a book during his vacation but has trouble getting started.
Rob sees a flying saucer but nobody believes him.
